references.text: Jesus' first prediction of suffering in Luke, where he says that the Son of Man must suffer greatly and be rejected – the same theme about the suffering of the Son of Man as in 9:44.

Jesus' third prediction of suffering in Luke, where he again tells the disciples that the Son of Man will be handed over (παραδοθήσεται) to the Gentiles – the same motif of being delivered into human hands.
The angels at the empty tomb remind the women that Jesus said the Son of Man had to be delivered into the hands of sinful men – a direct reference back to the words in 9:44.
Matthew's parallel to Jesus' prediction that the Son of Man will be handed over into human hands, with corresponding wording about παραδίδοσθαι εἰς χεῖρας ἀνθρώπων.
Mark's parallel suffering prediction where Jesus says that the Son of Man will be delivered into human hands – the closest parallel text to Luke 9:44.

God commands Moses to write this as a memorial – the expression "put these words in their ears" (Θέσθε εἰς τὰ ὦτα) has a parallel in Old Testament formulations about taking God's words to heart and remembering them.
Moses commands the people to put the words in their mouths and ears as a testimony – a linguistic parallel to Jesus' exhortation "Take these words to your hearts".
Samuel urges the people to pay attention to the words he has spoken – a similar exhortation to listen carefully to important words, as Jesus does in Luke 9:44.
Jesus says that the Son of Man is being handed over (παραδίδοται) into the hands of sinners, the fulfillment of the predictions about being delivered – including the one in Luke 9:44.
Peter proclaims that Jesus was handed over according to God's set plan and foreknowledge – a theological elaboration of what Jesus predicted in Luke 9:44 about being delivered.
